title: Multi-list task manager for Google Tasks refugees
one_liner: Give power users with dozens of lists fast list switching, archive/search, and painless migration off Google Tasks iOS regressions.

target_personas.name: Longtime Google Tasks power user (30–40 lists)
quotes: I’ve used Google Tasks for 10+ years, multiple times a day, with 30–40 lists
I’m now being forced to look for something different

target_personas.name: Multi-list iPad/iPhone task switcher
quotes: I need to find a new now because this is no longer efficient
For the biggest tech company this side of the Sun, it’s clunky, unreliable, not nearly as smooth and intuitive as gTasks

existing_solutions.name: Todoist
weaknesses: Migration of 30–40 Google Tasks lists still manual/frictionful
Not positioned as Google Tasks replacement with one-click import

existing_solutions.name: Apple Reminders / Things 3
weaknesses: Reminders weaker for many-list power workflows
Things is Apple-only and no Google Calendar parity for all users

existing_solutions.name: gTasks (third-party Google Tasks client)
weaknesses: Still depends on Google Tasks backend and API limits
Does not solve Google removing features server-side

product_hypothesis: MVP in 6–8 weeks: iOS-first task app with hierarchical/multi-list sidebar (restore the removed dropdown UX), full-text search, archive with timestamps, Google Tasks import + Google Calendar recurring sync, and a migration concierge checklist. Lead with App Store reviews citing hamburger/list regression; charge $4–8/mo or $40/yr for power-user sync.
research_notes: Nov 1 fullest-available rescan (HN+GitHub+App Store; PH/Reddit still tokenless) again yields a Google Tasks App Store echo: 8 of 20 merged posts sit in misc@google_tasks_get_things_done, citing multi-list nav regressions, missing archive/search, calendar sync breaks, and explicit switch intent. Raw ICE leaders are agent-memory (384→448 after enrich) and product-lifespan (336), but Stage 3 prioritizes the multi-member Tasks cluster over single-thread HN spikes. Caveats: single-product App Store dominance (enricher flags single-source echo), crowded task market, Google may restore UI, decade of lists = high switching cost. Next: interview switch-intent reviewers and test paid import waitlist before build.

confidence_basis.rationale: Eight App Store reviews on Google Tasks share multi-list UX regression and switch language; cluster also appeared in pipe_2026-10-30_001. Still one store/one product—medium confidence, validate not build+high.

evidence_ledger.claim: Longtime power users treat Google Tasks as a personal reference system and are being forced to look for alternatives after iOS list-menu removal.

evidence.quote: I’m now being forced to look for something different
I’ve used Google Tasks for 10+ years, multiple times a day, with 30–40 lists

assumptions: Users will pay for import+better list UX rather than wait for Google to restore the menu.

evidence_ledger.claim: Hamburger/list navigation regression creates explicit switch intent among multi-list users.

evidence.quote: I need to find a new now because this is no longer efficient

assumptions: Enough users will complete migration if import is one-click.

evidence_ledger.claim: Missing in-app search and archive keeps Completed lists congested versus the browser experience.

evidence.quote: Browser version works better because you can key word search, but not in the app

assumptions: Search+archive are table-stakes for paid power users.

evidence_ledger.claim: Users already compare Google Tasks unfavorably to third-party clients like gTasks.

evidence.quote: not nearly as smooth and intuitive as gTasks

assumptions: Willingness to try another client extends to leaving Google Tasks backend.

unsupported_assumptions: A new indie task app can win paid conversions against Todoist/Things solely on list UX.
Google will not restore the multi-list dropdown within one release cycle.
Users will trust an indie with decade-long personal reference data.

validation_required.experiment: Message 30 Google Tasks 1★ reviewers who mention lists/hamburger/switch; offer free guided import + $39/yr founding plan waitlist.
validation_required.success_criterion: ≥8 reply; ≥5 join waitlist; ≥3 complete import trial.

validation_required.experiment: Ship clickable prototype of multi-list sidebar + search/archive; 5 moderated usability tests with 20+ list users.
validation_required.success_criterion: ≥4/5 say they would switch within 30 days if import works.

switching_cost.rationale: Decade of lists and personal reference data create high sunk cost and Google ecosystem lock-in; learning curve for another task app is moderate if import works.

current_workarounds: Using browser Google Tasks for search
Third-party clients like gTasks still on Google backend
workaround_analysis.rationale: Workarounds are clumsy; browser search helps but mobile regressions remain; gTasks does not remove Google dependency.

buyer_mapping.user: Individual power user living in Google Tasks daily
buyer_mapping.buyer: Same individual on personal App Store / subscription card
buyer_mapping.champion: Longtime user publicly writing 1★ switch-intent reviews

persistence.rationale: Looks like Google consumer-app neglect (start ok, weak long-term polish). Platform could restore UI, so not structural_permanent; history suggests slow/no fix—treat as unknown/platform-owned until Google response is observed.

economic_impact.quantification_notes: Primarily daily friction minutes for multi-list navigation and broken recurring calendar sync—not direct B2B revenue loss. Paid WTP likely $3–8/mo for power users if migration is trusted.
